title: Maharashtra FDA Suspends Domino's and Five Other Eatery Licences Over Food Safety Violations
excerpt: A statewide enforcement drive found cockroach infestations, expired ingredients, and missing safety documentation across six food establishments in Maharashtra.
body:
• Maharashtra's Food and Drug Administration suspended licences of six food establishments, including Domino's outlets, over hygiene and safety violations.
  • Inspectors found cockroach infestations, expired food stock, misbranded products, and absence of employee health records.
  • The action was part of a statewide drive that saw 31 inspections and seizure of banned products worth Rs 34.87 lakh.
  • Nineteen people were arrested for selling banned pan masala and gutkha during the enforcement operation.

Maharashtra's Food and Drug Administration has suspended the food business licences of six establishments, including Domino's outlets, after inspectors uncovered cockroach infestations, expired ingredients, misbranded products, and a string of hygiene violations during a statewide enforcement drive.

The action forms part of a broader crackdown by the Maharashtra FDA, which conducted 31 inspections across the state over a three-day window. FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe has emphasized that no establishment is above scrutiny, targeting both small local eateries and global fast-food chains.

What Inspectors Found

"The action was part of a statewide drive that saw 31 inspections and seizure of banned products worth Rs 34.87 lakh."

The violations documented across the six suspended establishments ranged from structural to operational. Inspectors reported active cockroach and rat infestations in food preparation areas, unhygienic storage of raw ingredients with high cross-contamination risk, and kitchen stock stored well past its expiration date. Several outlets lacked employee health check-up records, and none had a functioning customer grievance redressal mechanism, as required under FSSAI regulations.

At one establishment, inspectors seized misbranded food products valued at Rs 11,350 and confiscated expired stock worth Rs 16,201, which was destroyed on-site.

A Wider Enforcement Push

The restaurant suspensions are part of an increasingly assertive food safety posture by the Maharashtra FDA. The same enforcement drive saw the seizure of banned tobacco products — primarily gutkha and pan masala — valued at Rs 34.87 lakh. Officials arrested 19 individuals for involvement in the sale and transportation of prohibited food items, sealed one establishment, and impounded three transport vehicles.

The crackdown follows earlier FDA action against McDonald's outlets in Ahmednagar over cheese labeling violations, and inspections at prominent Mumbai clubs including the Cricket Club of India and Willingdon Sports Club, where inspectors found live cockroaches, moldy ingredients, and structural decay in kitchens.

Global Chains Under the Microscope

The FDA has signaled that inspections will continue across all major global fast-food outlets in the state, including KFC, Pizza Hut, and Burger King. The focus extends beyond hygiene to product labeling, particularly whether cheese alternatives are being used in products advertised as containing real cheese.

For diaspora visitors accustomed to stringent food safety standards abroad, the enforcement drive reflects a growing push by Indian regulators to hold food businesses — both local and international — to FSSAI compliance standards that were often loosely enforced in the past. The FDA has said it will continue surprise inspections and take legal action against businesses found violating food safety norms.

nri_angle: The crackdown on major food chains raises awareness for Indian Americans who frequent these brands during visits to India and highlights the growing push for food safety enforcement in the country.
